A1.justification: Both readable ten-page PDFs describe the same DeepDeblurRF work and support comparison of text, mathematics, figures and tables. Neither includes an appendix or the separately referenced supplementary material; judgments cover the supplied PDFs.

before.justification: Section 5 reports original novel-view synthesis experiments, runtime measurements and iteration ablations in Tables 1–3 and accompanying figures.

after.justification: Section 5 retains these original benchmark results, runtime measurements and iteration ablations.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains NAFNet initialization, COLMAP pose estimation, alternating radiance field construction and RF-guided deblurring, and the Plenoxels and 3D Gaussian variants.

E1.justification: Both use BlurRF-Synth, BlurRF-Real, Deblur-NeRF real scenes and BlurRF-SB, retaining the same motion-blur, defocus, low-light and shared-blur-direction coverage.

E2.justification: Corresponding comparisons retain Deblur-NeRF, BAD-NeRF, DP-NeRF, ExBluRF, PDRF-10, Deblurring-3DGS and BAGS. Their participation in each reported comparison is unchanged.

E3.justification: Sections 4–5 retain the same splits, sample counts, blur synthesis, evaluation metrics and experimental settings, including N = 5 and the GPU conditions for timing.

E4.justification: The BlurRF-SB robustness comparison and N = 1–6 iteration ablation remain unchanged in Tables 2–3 and Figures 7–8. No additional analysis is included.

E5.justification: Both report the same point estimates without repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: Tables 1–3, plotted results and qualitative examples are unchanged. The added sentence pointing to more experimental results in supplementary material supplies no new results within v2.pdf.

T1.justification: Section 3 retains the same image and radiance-field definitions and unknown-degradation assumption. No mathematical reasoning, derivation or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution bullets and conclusion retain the same claims about RF-guided iterative deblurring, representation compatibility, BlurRF-Synth, synthesis quality and reduced training time.

C2.justification: The multiview-aggregation and learned-prior explanations remain unchanged, as do the reference-image caveats and the limitation concerning blur more severe than the training data.

D1.justification: Implementation disclosures, including Adam parameters, learning-rate scheduling, pruning intervals and hardware, are unchanged. Existing supplementary-detail pointers remain; no new technical detail or access resource is supplied.

R1.justification: Both retain the same 45 references and the same discussion of prior methods, their limitations and DeepDeblurRF's positioning.

P1.justification: v2 updates affiliations to KT and POSTECH, adds a work-at-POSTECH footnote and funding acknowledgements, and adds one supplementary-results pointer. The scientific prose and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: All eight figures and three tables retain their content, captions and designs. Spacing and column/page breaks change modestly, including the conclusion continuing onto page 9 and the references reflowing.

improvement.justification: v2 adds affiliation and funding information but leaves the scientific argument, evidence, reproducibility details and limitations unchanged. The supplementary-results pointer adds no assessable evidence, and the modest layout changes produce no meaningful overall quality difference.
